items.title: آنچه گذشت؛ انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای آمریکا ۲۰۲۶
items.summary: محسن رضایی در نخستین واکنش به نتایج انتخابات کنگره در آمریکا گفته است مقاومت ایران در جنگ موجب شده دونالد ترامپ «در میدان نبرد، تنگه هرمز و واشنگتن» شکست بخورد. ترامپ با اشاره به اظهارات جی‌دی ونس، معاونش، گفت که تاثیر جنگ بر شکست جمهوری‌خواهان تا حد زیادی درست است. جی دی ونس در اظهاراتی که بسیاری آن را در تضاد با سیاست‌ها و برنامه کاخ سفید خوانده‌اند، گفته علت شکست جمهوری‌خواهان در انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای، جنگ با ایران بود.

items.title: «پایان جنگ با ایران»؛ یکی از سه اولویت اصلی دموکرات‌ها در کنگره آمریکا
items.summary: دموکرات‌های آمریکا پس از پیروزی در انتخابات کنگره، پایان دادن به جنگ با ایران، کاهش فشار هزینه‌های زندگی و پاسخگو کردن دولت ترامپ را سه اولویت اصلی خود اعلام کرده‌اند. رهبران دموکرات می‌گویند که کنگره دیگر تابع دولت ترامپ نخواهد بود. در مقابل، جمهوری‌خواهان پس از یکی از سنگین‌ترین شکست‌های انتخاباتی خود، با چالش آینده حزب و فاصله گرفتن برخی متحدان نزدیک ترامپ، از جمله جی‌دی ونس، روبه‌رو هستند. نتایج انتخابات همچنین پرسش‌هایی درباره آینده جنبش «ماگا»، برگرفته از شعار انتخاباتی ترامپ «عظمت را دوباره به آمریکا بازگردانیم»، مطرح کرده است.

items.summary_original: A U.S. Marine died Tuesday after an incident during training at Camp Schwab in Okinawa, Japan, military officials said. The incident happened in Okinawa, on a Marine Corps base near the northeastern coast of Okinawa Prefecture. The Marine, who was identified as Lance Cpl. Devin J. Hernandez, 25, of Maryland, was with the 3rd Marine Division. ALLEGED KILLING BY MARINE PROMPTS US MILITARY TO RESTRICT OFF-BASE LIBERTY IN OKINAWA "It is with heavy hearts that 3rd Marine Division announces the death of a Marine following a training incident at Camp Schwab, Okinawa, Japan, on Nov. 3, 2026," the 3rd Marine Division said in a statement to ABC News. "We express our deepest condolences to the family and loved ones of our Marine." Hernandez was participating in fast-rope training at Camp Schwab when he sustained injuries during the training, the 3rd Marine Division said in a later statement to FOX News Digital. He was transported to a hospital and later succumbed to his injuries. The Marine's death remains under investigation, the 3rd Marine Division said. "The Marines and Sailors of 3rd Marine Division mourn the loss of one of our own. We extend our deepest condolences to Lance Cpl. Hernandez’s family, friends, and fellow Marines. "این فقط یک انتخابات میان دوره ای بد در سال 2006 نبود. این یک انکار در سطح واترگیت بود." ارزیابی صریح او پس از یک پیشرفت چشمگیر دموکرات ها در سنگرهای سنتی جمهوری خواهان در سراسر کشور، از جمله در ایالت خود، جایی که دموکرات ها هر سال پیروز شدند، صورت گرفت.
items.summary_original: Sen. Ted Cruz , R-Texas, delivered a scathing assessment on Wednesday of Republicans' sweeping midterm election losses, describing the results as a "blue tsunami" and warning that his party had lost touch with voters, particularly in the Lone Star State. In a lengthy post on X, Cruz acknowledged that Republicans had suffered historic defeats, losing control of both chambers of Congress while Democrats swept statewide races in Texas. "2026 was not simply a blue wave; it was a blue tsunami. It was an ass kicking," Cruz wrote. "It was not simply a bad 2006 midterm election. It was a Watergate-level repudiation." His blunt assessment came after a landmark Democratic breakthrough in traditionally Republican strongholds across the country, including in his home state, where Democrats won every statewide race, ending decades of Republican dominance. FLORIDA'S DESANTIS DESCRIBES GOP MIDTERMS WIPEOUT AS 'CLOSE TO AN EXTINCTION-LEVEL EVENT' FOR REPUBLICANS "Nowhere are the consequences of this election greater than Texas," Cruz wrote. "In the Lone Star State, we lost every single statewide election." "Texas is blue. That is a hard sentence to utter. But Texas, today at least, is blue," he continued. items.summary_original: Erika Kirk had a message for conservatives reeling from Republican election setbacks, and she turned to her late husband Charlie’s words to deliver it. "I miss Charlie so much every single day, but especially on a day like today," she wrote. "He always said that when things are going well, we need to stay humble. And when things aren’t going the way we want, we need to stay positive, keep our faith, and get back to work." ERIKA KIRK URGES CONSERVATIVE STUDENTS NOT TO BACK DOWN IN FIRST SCHOOL YEAR SINCE CHARLIE'S ASSASSINATION The widow of Turning Point USA CEO and founder Charlie Kirk said her husband had built a political operation meant to endure both victories and defeats. "Charlie’s vision for Turning Point Action was always bigger than one election," she wrote. "He wanted a permanent, year-round operation with the people, relationships, and resources to compete in every cycle. INSIDE CHARLIE KIRK’S EFFORT TO DEVELOP THE NEXT GENERATION OF CONSERVATIVE VOICES "He knew there would be victories and setbacks because he had experienced both and that’s why he built for both." items.summary: به گفته مقامات، یک زن کانادایی و دخترش در یک حمله مشکوک خرس گریزلی در آخر هفته هنگام پیاده روی در مسیری نزدیک خانه خود کشته شدند. جنیفر بالکاراس، 48 ساله، هنردرمانگر، و دخترش، سله رید، 20 ساله، روز شنبه پس از رفتن به پیاده روی در مسیر Snooka West Trail، تنها چند دقیقه از خانه خود در بلا کولا، بریتیش کلمبیا، ناپدید شدند. برادرش مت بالکاراس به The Vancouver Sun گفت که وقتی بالکاراس در یک جلسه آنلاین برنامه ریزی شده در روز شنبه حاضر نشد، عزیزان نگران شدند. راهنمای عملی برای اینکه خرس در تابستان امسال در حین پیاده‌روی یا کمپینگ مورد حمله قرار نگیرید پس از اینکه نتوانستند به این جفت برسند، بستگان از پلیس سواره سلطنتی کانادا (RCMP) خواستند تا یک بررسی رفاهی را در صبح یکشنبه انجام دهند. مقامات خودروی بالکاراس را که در آن پارک شده بود کشف کردند
items.summary_original: A Canadian woman and her daughter were killed in a suspected grizzly bear attack over the weekend while hiking on a trail near their home, according to authorities. Jennifer Balcarras, 48, an art therapist, and her daughter, Selah Reed, 20, went missing Saturday after going for a walk on the Snooka West Trail, just minutes from their home in Bella Coola, British Columbia . Loved ones grew concerned when Balcarras failed to show up for a scheduled online meet-up on Saturday, her brother, Matt Balcarras, told The Vancouver Sun . A PRACTICAL GUIDE TO NOT GETTING MAULED BY A BEAR WHILE HIKING OR CAMPING THIS SUMMER After failing to reach the pair, relatives asked the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) for a welfare check on Sunday morning. Authorities discovered Balcarras' vehicle parked at the trailhead . Her body was recovered Monday, and search teams found Reed's body on Tuesday. GRIZZLY BEAR MAULS HIKER, DRAGS HIM DOZENS OF FEET ON GLACIER NATIONAL PARK TRAIL "There was evidence to suggest a bear may have been involved," Jeff Tyre, an inspector with the British Columbia Conservation Officer Service, said in a video update posted to social media. Tyre noted that officers were actively working to "locate and capture any bears involved" and said it was not immediately clear if more than one animal was responsible. While Republicans held their ground in Florida, winning the governor's mansion , the Senate race, and maintaining their 20-8 edge in the US House, nationally the GOP got crushed under the weight of a blue tsunami. items.summary_original: EXCLUSIVE: Vice President JD Vance is seeking to forge a new alliance with disaffected Trump voters ahead of the 2028 election cycle, Fox News Digital has learned. Vance took control of his own messaging Wednesday morning in the wake of a brutal Republican midterm beatdown, breaking with President Donald Trump on foreign policy and America's relationship with Israel. A source familiar with post-election happenings told Fox News Digital that there was a White House meeting Wednesday morning aimed at aligning the entire administration officials on post-midterm messaging. A second source familiar described the meeting as a regular senior staff meeting. VANCE'S SCATHING IRAN WAR POSTMORTEM PUTS POTENTIAL 2028 GOP SHOWDOWN IN FOCUS: 'EVERYONE KNOWS WHY' "The reason we lost is the war," Vance's post said. "The president himself said so last night." "If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest," he went on. "But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there." In the post, Vance said a pollster and "one of the smartest people I know in politics" laid out four tasks that would bring voters back to the GOP — end the war in Iran, focus on the cost of living and inflation, put America first , and "change our relationship with Israel." items.summary_original: After the midterm elections , attention will turn to the 2028 race for the White House. What is on voters’ minds as they look ahead to the next presidential election? Most Republicans want the next president to follow President Donald Trump’s policies, if not his style. Nearly 4 in 10 MAGA Republicans want Trump’s successor to emulate both, and about half want the next president to follow his policies alone. Non-MAGA Republicans are less enthusiastic: 45% want his policies to continue, but only about 15% of non-MAGA Republicans want a president with the same style. Independents prefer something entirely different: 6 in 10 want the next president to break with both Trump’s policies and his style. Likewise, few Democrats want to see either his style or his policies repeated. Even as the Democrats have won control of the Senate and the House of Representatives, and Trump finds his approval rating at 39%, a bloc of voters remains loyal to the president and is likely to influence the 2028 campaign. While half of voters want a successor who does not emulate his style or follow his policies, 26% want a president who will carry on his policies, and another 12% want the next president to copy his policies and his style. items.summary_original: President Donald Trump stood by War Secretary Pete Hegseth Wednesday, saying he was doing "a very good job" even as current and former administration figures continued to question how long the Pentagon chief could remain in his post after Republicans’ bruising midterm losses. "I think he’s doing a very good job," Trump said Wednesday when asked by the media whether he was considering replacing Hegseth. The public support came a day after Democrats secured majorities in both chambers of Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections, setting the stage for a shift in power on Capitol Hill in January. The Iran war and its economic fallout loomed large in the election, with Hegseth among the administration's most vocal advocates for the campaign. His future remains the subject of speculation among current and former administration figures despite Trump's public backing. Although the secretary of state's election results show it on the path to defeat as of Wednesday afternoon, the DSA’s support for the policy has created a flashpoint for larger discussions about socialism's redistributive aims and the capital flight critics say could follow. "In their mind, every tax they do is some attempt to get money from people who create wealth and move it to the state," Richard Stern, an economics scholar with Advancing American Freedom (AAF), said in an interview with Fox News Digital. The DSA's stance on Proposition 40 has also brought it into conflict with other Democratic figures, including Gov. Gavin Newsom , who opposed it. To prevent billionaires from simply leaving the state, Proposition 40 was designed to retroactively apply to billionaires who were residents of California on Jan. 1, 2026. items.summary_original: Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., is officially running to be Speaker of the House in the next Congress. It comes after Democrats made historic gains in Tuesday night's midterm elections, taking back both the House and Senate for the remainder of President Donald Trump's term. Jeffries sent a letter to fellow House Democrats on Wednesday afternoon congratulating them on their victories and adding, "I write to humbly request your support in connection with my candidacy to serve as the next Speaker of the House of Representatives." Jeffries told reporters that he intended to run for the top job in the House during a press conference with his top deputies on Wednesday, House Minority Whip Katherine Clark, D-Mass., and House Democratic Caucus Chairman Pete Aguilar, D-Calif. DEMOCRAT SEIZE HOUSE CONTROL IN STUNNING BLUE TSUNAMI, VOW RETRIBUTION AGAINST TRUMP ADMIN Clark and Aguilar also signaled they would run for the No. 2 and No. 3 positions in the House. And despite a small group of far-left socialists elected to Congress who are expected to pose a headache for Jeffries and other establishment Democrats, he will likely have little trouble winning the speaker's gavel given the wide majority his party won on Tuesday. At the time of writing this story, Democrats were projected to win 237 seats compared to 139 for the GOP. But 59 races are still too close to call, and Jeffries told reporters earlier that he anticipated a total of 255 or more Democrats in the House next year.

items.summary_original: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani scored a legal victory Wednesday after a state appeals court reversed a lower court ruling that had ordered his administration to redo the rollout of a tax on high-end second homes. The four-judge panel unanimously dismissed the homeowners' lawsuit, finding that the plaintiffs lacked legal standing. The decision overturned a September ruling by a Staten Island judge who had ordered the city to restart the tax's implementation. The ruling allows Mamdani's administration to continue implementing the surcharge — also known as a pied-à-terre tax — a key part of his agenda to raise taxes on wealthy New Yorkers and help close the city's budget gap. The tax still faces separate legal challenges. NYC JUDGE ORDERS MAMDANI TO REDO SECOND-HOME TAX ROLLOUT The surcharge, approved by the New York state Legislature in May, applies to qualifying second homes valued at $5 million or more for one- to three-family properties and $1 million or more for condos and co-ops. The city's Department of Finance sent initial determination notices to approximately 17,000 property owners in July. A Staten Island judge ruled Sept. 29 that the city had mishandled the rollout and ordered officials to restart the process . The city appealed while continuing to implement the tax. items.summary_original: Democratic heavyweights Gavin Newsom and Marc Elias are mobilizing behind Scott Colom as the Mississippi Senate race remains too close to call, with the California governor soliciting emergency donations and Elias’ law firm preparing for a legal fight over the final count. In an overnight fundraising email obtained by Fox News Digital, Newsom’s campaign told supporters, "Please help asap," warning that the race was entering "a phase of ballot curing and possible legal fights." Elias said his firm is "leading the legal effort to ensure" Colom wins. "As you read this, Scott leads the Republican incumbent by just a couple hundred votes," the email said. "There is no way Republicans are giving up this Senate seat without a fight. The job is not finished!" DEMS SEIZE THE SENATE AS BLUE TIDAL WAVE CRASHES DEEP INTO TRUMP COUNTRY, TOPPLES GOP STRONGHOLDS The Mississippi Senate race between Colom and incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, R-Miss., remained uncalled Wednesday because thousands of ballots had yet to be processed. Colom led Hyde-Smith by just 43 votes in incomplete, unofficial results, while an estimated 44,000 ballots remained outstanding, including absentee, affidavit and provisional ballots. They are Adam Hamilton of Kansas; Julia Stratton of Illinois; Troy Jackson of Maine; Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota; and Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan. The first time earned her a rare public rebuke from Jeffries, who called it a "breach of trust." Other left-wing lawmakers called for her to be removed from the powerful House Appropriations Committee over the move. items.summary_original: Outgoing Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said Wednesday that the Republican losses in the midterm elections are "close to an extinction-level event" for the party "in many parts of the country, as we have seen probably in the last 100 years." DeSantis spoke after Republicans lost control of both the House and Senate on Election Day. Rep. Byron Donalds, a Florida House Republican, won the contest for DeSantis' seat despite other GOP candidates losing their gubernatorial races around the U.S. "Here's the thing. Democrats are unpopular. They were able to win based off the sentiment that exists in the country right now. They did not earn a mandate to indulge all their left-wing fantasies. And they're going to be in there governing, and we'll see what ends up happening," DeSantis said. "But this was not a positive view of the Democrats. This was a rejection of Republicans in Washington," he added. "And Democrats just happened to be the beneficiary." TRUMP-BACKED BYRON DONALDS MAKES HISTORY AS FLORIDA'S FIRST BLACK GOVERNOR DeSantis, who has not ruled out a 2028 presidential bid, said, "In January, when everyone in office leaves, who were either term-limited or got voted out of the 10 largest states in this union, only one state will have Republican control of their state, the state of Florida. items.summary_original: In the weeks leading up to Election Day, President Donald Trump repeatedly railed against public opinion polls that pointed to a potential blue wave for the Democrats in the midterms. "I think it’s fake polls," the president argued. "A lot of the polls are rigged." It was an argument repeated by other top Republicans. "The polls are all wrong all around the country," House Speaker Mike Johnson emphasized Sunday at a Trump rally in Iowa. "I'm telling you, they're undercounting Republicans because Republicans are not participating in these polls anymore." HEAD HERE FOR FOX NEWS LIVE UPDATES ON THE MIDTERM ELECTIONS While public opinion polls have a history over the past decade of undercounting GOP voters — especially MAGA supporters — this time, pollsters say Democratic support, rather than Republican turnout, was underestimated. It was Democrats. "Polls probably, on average, undercounted Democrats significantly," veteran pollster Chris Anderson, the longtime Democratic partner on the Fox News Poll , said. Anderson, pointing to the massive blue wave that allowed Democrats to decisively recapture the House and Senate majorities in the midterms, told Fox News Digital, "This is sort of a seismic election and you can’t model for a seismic election. We definitely didn’t undercount Republicans, that’s for sure." items.summary_original: The much-touted "blue wave" came to fruition as Democrats won a stunning run of victories in both red and blue states. They also came out ahead in key governor’s races. The Fox News Voter Poll, a survey of more than 100,000 voters nationwide, highlights the central themes and demographic groups that defined these important races. STATE OF PLAY: BLUE WAVE SWEEPS DEMOCRATS INTO POWER, WITH KEY RACES STILL HANGING IN BALANCE Democrat Annie Andrews won a close-run race against incumbent Republican Darline Graham to flip a Senate seat that had been in the hands of Graham’s brother Lindsey for more than 20 years. Appointed to the seat after her brother’s death in July, Graham underperformed his electoral strength; he won re-election to the Senate in 2020 by 11 percentage points. She also underperformed President Donald Trump’s strength among key groups from two years ago. Rural voters, for instance, backed Trump with 63% in 2024 – Graham this year garnered only 51%. Former Vice President Kamala Harris received 36% of the rural vote in 2024; Andrews bested that by about 10 points. Graham did manage to hang on to non-MAGA Republican voters, amid concerns that they would defect. But again, she got 70% of their vote, while Trump pulled in 79% two years ago. Independents: Andrews ran away among these voters, getting about 7 in 10. Trump received 39%, while Graham managed less than 20%. Andrews did well with women, college graduates and urban voters. items.summary_original: Florida Governor-elect Byron Donalds told Fox News on Wednesday that he believes Americans' frustrations about gas and diesel prices "boiled over" against Republicans on Election Day. The Trump-backed Florida House Republican made the remark after being asked by "Fox Friends" co-host Brian Kilmeade why he thinks so many people were unhappy with the first two years of the president's second term. The Democrats took back control of the House and Senate during the midterms , including flipping governor seats in states such as Texas, Georgia and Ohio. "I think, look, when you talk to people on the ground, gas prices are a major problem. I think people were looking at the price of gas, the price of diesel, and I think those frustrations boiled over," Donalds said. "I also want to look at, you know, in the United States Senate, there were some opportunities I think that were missed: not passing a Save America Act, not getting some of the key policies done, like putting through President Trump's border security packages and codifying that into law. I think that stuff frustrated Republicans," he continued. "I think if you not just look in Florida, but look around the country, what I'm starting to see is that we have a lot of Republicans who either did not vote or decided to go and vote for Democrats. On Monday, Netanyahu posted to X that "the public in Israel does not want a government that depends on Ra'am and the Joint List—parties that support terrorism and reject the existence of the Jewish state." items.summary: کی‌یف، اوکراین – رئیس‌جمهور اوکراین، ولودیمیر زلنسکی، درخواست‌های دولت ترامپ را برای توقف حمله به پالایشگاه‌های نفت روسیه از سوی نیروهای مسلح خود رد می‌کند و به فاکس نیوز گفت: «پاسخ ما باید دردناک باشد». زلنسکی در مصاحبه ای در کیف اذعان کرد که مذاکراتی با دولت ترامپ درباره هدف قرار دادن تاسیسات نفتی داشته است، حملاتی که دونالد ترامپ، رئیس جمهور آمریکا آنها را تا حدودی مقصر قیمت های بالای گاز در ایالات متحده می داند. ما گفتیم که اگر می‌خواهید به پالایشگاه‌های روسیه حمله نکنیم، آنها مجبور نیستند به سیستم انرژی ما حمله کنند.» ترامپ به زلنسکی می‌گوید در طول حملات به روسیه از انجام «یک کار» دست بکشد اوکراین نزدیک به روز گزارش داده است.
items.summary_original: KYIV, Ukraine — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is defying calls from the Trump administration for his armed forces to stop attacking Russian oil refineries, telling Fox News: "Our response must be painful." In an interview in Kyiv, Zelenskyy acknowledged holding discussions with the Trump administration about targeting oil facilities, attacks President Donald Trump has pinned as being partly to blame for high gas prices in the U.S. "We had different conversations — different, and several — with President Trump and with his team about attacks on refineries," Zelenskyy said. "We said that if you want us not to attack Russia's refineries, they have not to attack our energy system." TRUMP TELLS ZELENSKYY TO STOP DOING 'ONE THING' DURING ATTACKS ON RUSSIA Ukraine has reported near-daily Russian strikes on energy infrastructure , triggering power outages just as temperatures dip ahead of winter. "That's why we have to respond. But our response has to be painful for Russian military people," Zelenskyy said. "If we will not respond on energy, they will continue." U.S.-Ukraine relations took a further hit in October when Trump struck a deal to import millions of tons of Russian diesel to the United States. INSIDE MELANIA MELANIA'SPLATICLETRUET نوشت: "ایالات متحده در مذاکرات سطح کاری بین اوکراین و روسیه در 10 تا 11 نوامبر در ابوظبی میانجیگری خواهد کرد و ماموریت پرزیدنت ترامپ برای پایان دادن به جنگ را پیش می برد. بحث ها بر ترتیبات امنیتی پس از جنگ، کاهش تنش، تلاش های بشردوستانه و گام های بعدی به سمت صلح متمرکز خواهد بود." توافق آتش بس روسیه و اوکراین پیش از مذاکرات صلح هفته آینده، مذاکره کنندگان آمریکایی این هفته در بروس دیدار خواهند کرد.
items.summary_original: U.S. officials will mediate a new round of talks between Ukraine and Russia next week with the goal of delivering "lasting security for generations to come," U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff said on Monday. Witkoff said the U.S.-mediated negotiations will be held on Nov. 10 and 11 in Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates. "The United States will mediate working-level negotiations between Ukraine and Russia on November 10–11 in Abu Dhabi, advancing President Trump’s mission to end the war. Discussions will focus on post-war security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts, and next steps toward peace," Witkoff wrote on X. "Additionally, American negotiators will meet this week in Brussels with representatives from France, Germany, the United Kingdom, the EU, and NATO to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine, Europe’s post-war security architecture, and economic opportunities to support Ukraine’s reconstruction," Witkoff said. items.summary_original: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned Monday that Russia is preparing a "massive attack" on Ukraine centered on Tuesday's midterm elections in the United States, accusing Moscow of seeking to exploit the historical vote to unleash strikes while the world's attention is elsewhere. The Ukrainian leader's warning came as voters prepared to decide which party controls Congress, a result that could also influence Washington's future response to Russian President Vladimir Putin's almost five-year war in Ukraine. In a post on X, Zelenskyy went on to urge the Trump administration to increase pressure on Moscow, warning that Russia could exploit the elections to target Ukraine's battered energy infrastructure and supply routes. DRONE STRIKE SINKS SHIP IN NATO WATERS AS ZELENSKYY WARNS OF LOOMING ‘MASSIVE STRIKE’ "We have intel that Russia is preparing a new massive attack on our country – primarily targeting energy and logistics," Zelenskyy said in his nightly address. "The assumption is basically that tomorrow the world will be watching the American midterms, and what is happening here in Ukraine, along with our difficulties with air defense and Patriot missiles, will be overlooked." Zelenskyy's warning came hours after Russian forces struck a school being used to distribute humanitarian aid in Komyshuvakha, a settlement in southeastern Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region. items.summary_original: Friday’s late-night confrontation at Poland's Constitutional Tribunal, which drew riot police and protesters and prompted President Karol Nawrocki to turn his plane around and return to Warsaw, has reignited a bitter debate over whether Prime Minister Donald Tusk is restoring the rule of law or overstepping constitutional limits. The dispute erupted after the tribunal announced the suspension of its president, Bogdan Święczkowski, a move that supporters of Tusk’s government described as necessary to restore judicial independence, while critics denounced it as an unconstitutional power grab. Marcin Przydacz, the head of the International Policy Bureau in Nawrocki’s office, took to European TV Monday morning denouncing Tusk’s actions, saying, "Even lawyers who are close to the Tusk government say that there's absolutely no legal basis for such behavior." POLISH PRESIDENT TURNS PLANE AROUND AFTER 'COUP' AT NATION’S TOP COURT The dispute is also triggering diplomatic fallout, with at least three Polish ambassadors resigning in protest. Przydacz, a former parliament member of the now-opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party, says Poland’s permanent representative to the U.N. since 2021, Krzysztof Szczerski, resigned Monday, which followed the resignations over the weekend of the ambassadors to China and Romania. items.summary_original: Ukraine officials said the country’s official air-raid alert app was likely hacked after emergency alerts warned on Sunday that there was a "radiation hazard" and a "chemical attack alert" in Kyiv. The false warnings urged residents not to go outside. "There is a radiation hazard alert in Kyiv. Do not go outside!" read one alert. RUSSIA LAUNCHES BALLISTIC MISSILE ATTACK ON KYIV HOURS AFTER ZELENSKYY WARNS OF MAJOR STRIKE "There is a chemical attack alert in Kyiv. Do not go outside!" another one read. The public air alert online map also displayed Kyiv and other areas as under a nuclear alert. The app also issued false warnings about Russia’s hypersonic Oreshnik missile and alleged street fighting in Kyiv. Additionally, loudspeakers in the streets blasted a recorded message instructing people to take precautions. But Ukraine’s Air Force said its air alert app was hacked and that there was no radiation hazard to be concerned about. "The air alert app appears to have been subjected to enemy influence. There is no radiation threat! Stay calm and follow our updates on our channel!" the Ukrainian Air Force said in a statement posted to Telegram. Ukraine’s Center for Strategic Communications blamed Russia for the incident, although no group had publicly claimed responsibility. United Against Nuclear Iran (UANI), which conducted the months-long probe, said at least nine similar tankers carrying Iranian oil or LPG have also evaded U.S. restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz since Washington reinstated the Iranian port blockade in July. UANI identified one of the sanctioned tankers as the SOGL. It allegedly escaped the blockade on Sept. 1 carrying approximately 500,000 barrels of Iranian LPG after collecting it at an Iranian port in August. The vessel then traveled thousands of miles to a Malaysian offshore anchorage, where UANI filmed the vessel receiving fuel and other services offshore. The ship then traveled on to China, where the organization said it discharged its Iranian cargo. items.summary_original: President Abelardo de la Espriella means business when it comes to his war against the cartels. Colombia's new president, known by the nickname of "El Tigre." was voted in on a law-and-order ticket and so far his actions in fighting the cartels are seemingly paying dividends — not just in Colombia but in Washington, too. Recently, he arrived at the Barranquilla police command around the early hours of the morning as 587 police officers and soldiers raided 50 locations across the Caribbean port city and its suburbs in Operation Blindaje 360. A few days earlier, domestic Colombian news outlets had widely publicized a recording intercepted by Colombian police of "Keko," the alleged leader of a gang called "Los del Freseo," boasting that de la Espirella had nothing on him. "The Tiger's got nothing. Let him come out, and we'll put lead in him," Keko allegedly said on the recording. Then, before dawn, Colombia's president had tracked him down and was face to face with him, all caught on tape. According to a video released by his presidential office, El Tigre told Keko the gang leader was "a tough guy on the phone… but the look of the fear on his face matched that of his many victims." The sweep ended with 72 arrests. items.summary_original: The U.S. Embassy in Moscow issued a security alert Saturday warning people of a potential "mass casualty event" at the 2 Museum Reserve in Moscow. "The U.S. Embassy in Moscow is aware of a credible threat of a mass casualty event TODAY October 31, at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in Moscow at Dolskaya Ulitsa 1, Moscow, Russia 11569. The U.S. government is coordinating with appropriate Russian authorities on a response," the embassy wrote in a statement. The alert warned people to avoid the Tsaritsyno Museum area and to "stay alert, and avoid crowds." Founded in 1775 as a summer home for Russia's Catherine II, the Tsaritsyno Museum is now a popular tourist attraction in Russia's capital. INSIDE MELANIA TRUMP'S SECRET DIPLOMATIC ROLE IN THE RUSSIA-UKRAINE CEASEFIRE DEAL The museum itself attracted more than 2 million visitors in 2022, Moscow's deputy mayor, Natalya Sergunina, said in 2023. The surrounding grounds, enjoyed by Moscow's local citizens for physical activity and dog walking, get even more foot traffic, according to The Art Newspaper. The U.S. Embassy's alert also included a warning to people in the Moscow area to keep cellphone batteries and other batteries charged, remain aware of surroundings and review a personal security plan. The alert was issued as tensions in the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine continue to escalate. items.summary_original: The French government is deploying 70,000 police officers to cities across the country as authorities expect a third week of intense anti-government protests to resume Saturday. Demonstrators objecting to rising costs and President Emmanuel Macron's government have engaged in looting and damaging property, prompting the law enforcement surge, according to officials. "Everyone is on deck to ensure an extremely firm response to any trouble," Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said at a news conference early in the week. FRANCE ON EDGE WITH 70,000 POLICE DEPLOYED FOR UNREST AS AUTHORITIES PROBE SUSPECTED TERROR ATTACK NEAR PARIS The expected protests, coinciding with Halloween, introduce an additional element to authorities' response, and some protesters are expected to don Halloween masks to hide their identities. At least 150 planned gatherings across the country have been tracked and acknowledged by the Interior Ministry. Videos circulating on social media Saturday appeared to show fresh confrontations as anti-government protests continued across France despite the deployment of 70,000 police officers nationwide. In Paris, video posted to X by journalist Oliya Scootercaster appeared to show an object being thrown toward a group of riot police as officers moved through a street. items.summary_original: While en route to Senegal, Poland’s President Karol Nawrocki turned his plane around and returned home after police entered Poland's top court, the Constitutional Tribunal, and the tribunal’s president was suspended. "At such a moment, the President must be in Poland," Nawrocki posted on X . "I'm interrupting my flight to Senegal. I'm returning." Police say they secured the Tribunal after dozens of protesters gathered to demonstrate against what they called the wrongful suspension of the top court’s president by the current pro-European government. Police said there were also dangerous objects thrown at officers outside the building. Some protesters outside the court were seen praying, while others held posters reading "Tusk — a symbol of anti-Polish sentiment," "Down with the commies and Tusk’s regime," and "Stop destroying the state." Poland’s top judicial bodies, including the Constitutional Tribunal, have been a major bone of contention between the current pro-European government, led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk, and the main opposition party, national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), which ruled the country from 2015 to 2023. Critics accuse the PiS of imposing political control over key judicial institutions, with some reforms having led the EU to impose fines on Poland. items.summary_original: Israel's final election count has confirmed that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc has lost its parliamentary majority, but whether opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot can assemble a government to replace him remains an open question as negotiations begin behind closed doors. The completed count, published early Friday by Israel's Central Elections Committee , gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for Eisenkot's opposition alliance. The two predominantly Arab parties secured a historic 19 seats, placing them in a potentially decisive position. Netanyahu's Likud emerged as the largest individual party with 27 seats, followed by Eisenkot's Yashar with 21 and former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett's Beyachad with 12. Final voter turnout reached 77.9%, according to the Central Elections Committee results . Members of the main opposition Democratic Party also blocked access to the podium during a vote on a central bank bill, Reuters reported. "These ruling lawmakers are criminals, and they deserve tear gas, rubber bullets, cracked skulls, and broken bones—not the young people," opposition leader Sali Berisha declared during a speech before his microphone was cut off. SERBIA’S STUDENT MOVEMENT TOPPLES VUCIC’S PARTY AFTER 14 YEARS, BUT POLITICAL AGENDA REMAINS UNCLEAR As the chamber devolved into chaos, fellow opposition members surrounded Berisha, holding blue flares, the official color of their party, and displaying images of protesters injured by police rubber bullets. Albania has been gripped in recent weeks by student-led demonstrations demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama over alleged government corruption, underfunded schools, widespread unemployment, and a lack of economic opportunities. items.summary_original: TEL AVIV, Israel - Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's governing coalition remained well short of a parliamentary majority Thursday as newly counted ballots showed a dramatic surge in support for Arab parties, potentially giving the opposition enough votes to challenge his control of parliament. With 93.8% of ballots counted as of 4 a.m. ET Thursday (10 a.m. local time in Israel), including votes from the double-envelope count, Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc was projected to win 53 seats in Israel's 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for the opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot. The two predominantly Arab parties were projected to secure a combined 19 seats, bringing the potential anti-Netanyahu parliamentary majority to 67. The updated figures showed Netanyahu's Likud remaining the largest individual party with 26 seats, followed by Eisenkot's Yashar party with 21 and former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett's Beyachad party with 12. The figures remain preliminary. NETANYAHU DEFIES EXIT POLLS AS VOTE SHIFTS IN HIS FAVOR, BUT MAJORITY REMAINS ELUSIVE The results leave neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot with the 61 seats required to form a government independently, raising the prospect of difficult coalition negotiations or another election. The biggest shift came from Israel's Arab voters, whose turnout surged compared with previous elections, potentially reshaping the country's political balance. The two parties were projected to win a combined 19 Knesset seats, according to preliminary results. However, both Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud-led right-wing bloc and the opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot’s centrist bloc fell short of the 61 seats needed for a parliamentary majority. On Wednesday, Prime Minister Netanyahu wrote on X that Israel’s election had been "stolen by Arab parties that support terrorism and the elimination of the Jewish state," alleging serious criminal offenses, including bribery, threats, violence, forgery and the use of prohibited software to mobilize voters. "We write to express concern about the state of democracy and the rule of law in the Republic of Albania, a NATO ally and candidate for European Union membership. The United States has invested heavily in Albania's justice reforms and has a strong interest in their success. Recent events suggest that progress is fragile and, in key areas, at risk of reversal," the letter to Secretary Rubio said. Specifically, the letter urges Secretary Rubio to use the State Department's authority under Section 7031(c) of the annual Department of State, Foreign Operations and Related Programs Appropriations Act to publicly designate Albanian officials and their immediate family members, if necessary, if credible information of involvement in significant corruption exists. items.summary: تصمیم دولت بریتانیا برای پذیرش اقدامات گسترده برای مقابله با یهودی ستیزی در مدارس، تضاد شدیدی با استراتژی اخیراً رونمایی شده شهردار نیویورک، زهران ممدانی، ایجاد می‌کند و این سؤال را ایجاد می‌کند که چرا طرح بریتانیا خاص‌تر از طرح پیشنهادی در یهودی‌نشین‌ترین شهر آمریکا به نظر می‌رسد. دولت بریتانیا تمام 27 توصیه از یک بررسی مستقل در مورد یهودی ستیزی در مدارس و کالج های انگلستان را پذیرفت. این اقدامات شامل تشویق به تصویب تعریف کاری اتحاد بین المللی یادبود هولوکاست از یهودی ستیزی، آموزش تخصصی برای مربیان، تقویت روش های گزارش دهی و نظارت مستقل است. استراتژی 33 صفحه‌ای ممدانی - در حالی که فقط بر آموزش متمرکز نیست - در مقایسه، یک تعریف واحد از ضدها ارائه نمی‌کند.
items.summary_original: The British government’s decision to embrace sweeping measures addressing antisemitism in schools is drawing a sharp contrast with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s recently unveiled strategy, raising questions about why Britain’s plan appears more specific than the one proposed in America’s most Jewish city. The U.K. government accepted all 27 recommendations from an independent review into antisemitism in schools and colleges in England . The measures include encouraging adoption of the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance working definition of antisemitism, specialized training for educators, strengthened reporting procedures and independent oversight. Mamdani’s 33-page strategy — while not only focused on education — by comparison, does not adopt a single definition of antisemitism, explicitly address the relationship between anti-Zionism and antisemitism or establish numerical benchmarks for measuring whether its initiatives succeed. British Jewish author and Holocaust educator Dov Forman, who recently graduated from university, said Mamdani could learn from Britain’s targeted approach to addressing antisemitism in schools. items.summary: به گفته مقامات صربستان، اندکی بعد از نیمه شب چهارشنبه، یک مهاجم مسلح به دو چاقو به یکی از اعضای ژاندارمری صربستان که از سفارت اسرائیل در بلگراد محافظت می کرد، حمله کرد که باعث شد این افسر برای دفاع از خود به فرد مهاجم شلیک کند. ضارب که خردسال بود، فریاد زد «الله اکبر» یا به زبان عربی «خدا اکبر» در حالی که صورت افسر را برید و افسر را کمی مجروح کرد. ایویکا داچیچ، وزیر کشور، گفت که مقامات این حادثه را یک حمله تروریستی می دانند و افزود که نیروهای امنیتی مهاجم را زیر نظر داشتند. داچیچ گفت که مهاجم از داعش حمایت می کند و پرچم سیاهی را که نماد این گروه تروریستی را در خود دارد در حساب اینستاگرام خود به نمایش گذاشته است. داچیچ افزود، گمان می رود مهاجم صربستانی و اهل شهر ساباچ باشد.
items.summary_original: An assailant armed with two knives attacked a member of Serbia's Gendarmerie guarding the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade shortly after midnight Wednesday, prompting the officer to fatally shoot the attacker in self-defense, according to Serbian authorities. The assailant, who was a minor, allegedly shouted "Allahu Akbar" — or "God is great" in Arabic — as he slashed the officer in the face, leaving the officer "slightly injured." Interior Minister Ivica Dacic said authorities are treating the incident as a terrorist attack, adding that security forces had been monitoring the assailant. Dacic said the attacker supported ISIS and displayed a black flag bearing the terrorist group's symbol on his Instagram account. The attacker was believed to be Serbian and from the town of Sabac, Dacic added. HALIMA SALMAN CONVICTED OF RECEIVING ISIS MILITARY TRAINING IN SYRIA, FACES 10 YEARS IN PRISON Israel's foreign ministry confirmed the " attempted terrorist attack ," and said the incident was under investigation by the relevant authorities. "The attacker was neutralized by local police. No embassy personnel were injured, and the mission was closed at the time of the incident, which occurred late at night," the statement said. According to Serbian prosecutors, an unidentified person wearing black clothes opened the door to the security booth outside the embassy around 12:15 a.m. local time. items.title: بی‌طرفی، راستی‌آزمایی و پاسخ‌گویی؛ چرا بی‌بی‌سی فارسی بر این اصول ایستادگی می‌کند؟
items.summary: این مطلب توضیح می‌دهد که چرا بی‌بی‌سی فارسی در یکی از پرتنش‌ترین دوره‌های تاریخ معاصر ایران بر اصول بنیادین روزنامه‌نگاری، از جمله بی‌طرفی، راستی‌آزمایی، استقلال تحریریه و پاسخ‌گویی، پافشاری می‌کند. در این مقاله، با مرور شیوه تصمیم‌گیری‌های تحریریه، فرآیند راستی‌آزمایی اخبار، نحوه انتخاب مهمانان و برخورد با خطاها و انتقادها، تشریح می‌شود که هدف بی‌بی‌سی نه جانبداری از هیچ طرف، بلکه ارائه گزارشی دقیق، مستقل و مبتنی بر شواهد است تا مخاطبان بتوانند بر اساس اطلاعات قابل اعتماد، خود درباره رویدادها قضاوت کنند.

items.title: 'کودتای خزنده' در سپاه؛ نوار صوتی جلسه‌ای محرمانه در زمان جنگ
items.summary: با گذشت چهل سال از آغاز جنگ ایران و عراق، هنوز اطلاعات مرتبط با مقاطع مهمی از جنگ، از آرشیوهای محرمانه خارج نشده است. یکی از جلسات مهمی که در آن فرماندهی جنگ مورد انتقاد سپاهیان ناراضی قرار می‌گیرد، اوایل آذر ۶۳ برگزار می‌شود که در دهه‌های اخیر، رسانه‌های حکومتی ایران روایت‌های پراکنده و به‌شدت تحریف شده‌ای را از آن منتشر کرده‌اند.
